scope: Synthesizable bounded summary endpoint; full net ownership/transactions remain in the CPU controller
packet: Exact native persistent-shadow 64-byte payload, little-endian, unchanged kinds 1/2/3
topology: Immutable sorted unique global-node slots, u64 node:u32 + full SLR mask:u8 + reserved zero:u24. Lowest set bit is the owner; only shared boundary nodes are present.
storage: One owner-summary slot per node per logical-die CU, accessible only by that owner. One non-authoritative receiver record per lane/slot in each worker CU. Record u64 words: session, occupancy, history, version, topology entry, 0,0,0.
owner_install: Trusted controller supplies a committed summary. Kernel checks expected previous version, session, full membership and increasing version; same-version equal-value is idempotent. This does not calculate net-set occupancy or commit an entire net.
command: 128 bytes: packet followed by u64 descriptor words op:u32|lane:u32, slot, expected owner version for install only, 0,0,0,0,0
response: 128 bytes: packet (or fetched summary reply) followed by status, command ticket, op|lane<<32, slot, wrote_state,0,0,0
completion: 64 bytes: new command-read ticket, new response-write ticket, consumed count, launch_error, state writes, rejected commands, session,0
queue: Independent input/output ring capacities are powers of two <=2^20. Monotonic u64 tickets never wrap. Consume at most min(available commands, response credits, max_steps, remaining output ticket range). Invalid launch or no response credit causes no command consumption and no state mutation. Each consumed command returns one response, including rejected commands.
lifecycle: Controller owns buffers between launches and supplies strictly increasing sessions when resetting/checkpointing/changing slot mapping. Prior-session entries are logically absent; packets from a different current session are rejected. Uninitialized owner fetches fail rather than fabricating a zero summary.
interfaces: 512-bit separate AXI masters for ingress, owner state, receiver state and egress; 64-bit read-only topology master. Completion shares egress. Explicit U280 bank configuration exists but requires linked-platform evidence.
coherence: Controller owns buffers between launches. No host DMA or another CU may access a writable buffer while this CU owns it; responses become consumable after kernel completion. Owner installation/validation execute serially within a CU; cross-CU full-net atomicity is not implemented.
limits: No full router or whole-net hardware commit
No autonomous subscription scanner or inter-CU network scheduler
No simultaneous host producer/device consumer memory-coherence claim
No board performance, energy, or routed platform timing claim from HLS/cosim/hw_emu
C-model real-trace replay covers receiver/lookup; owner operations have separate directed RTL fixtures
